caseMetadata.caseName: Nexus Corp Ltd. v. Stark Industries Inc.

materialFacts: Nexus Corp Ltd. entered into a Commercial Supply Agreement with Stark Industries Inc. on Jan 1, 2024.
The Commercial Supply Agreement was governed by English law.
The agreement included an arbitration clause specifying London as the seat and UNCITRAL Rules.
Stark Industries Inc. failed to deliver vibranium cores by Dec 31, 2025.
Stark Industries Inc. claimed force majeure due to a global shortage as the reason for non-delivery.
Nexus Corp Ltd. claims breach of contract.
Nexus Corp Ltd. seeks $50M in damages.
Stark Industries Inc. claims the force majeure clause excuses performance.

chronology.event: Commercial Supply Agreement entered into between Nexus Corp Ltd. and Stark Industries Inc.
Deadline for Stark Industries Inc. to deliver vibranium cores; Stark Industries Inc. failed to deliver.

keyEvents: Failure of Stark Industries Inc. to deliver vibranium cores.
Stark Industries Inc. invoking force majeure.
Nexus Corp Ltd. claiming breach of contract and damages.

proceduralContext.proceduralPosture: Claim for breach of contract and damages in arbitration.
reliefSought: Excuse from performance (by Stark Industries Inc.)

arbitrationIndicators: IN THE ARBITRATION TRIBUNAL SEATED IN LONDON

explicit: Whether Stark Industries Inc. breached the Commercial Supply Agreement.
Whether Stark Industries Inc.'s non-performance is excused by the force majeure clause.
Whether Nexus Corp Ltd. is entitled to $50M in damages.
implicit: What constitutes 'force majeure' under the agreement and English law.
Whether a 'global shortage' qualifies as a force majeure event under the specific contract terms.
Whether Stark Industries Inc. took reasonable steps to mitigate the impact of the alleged force majeure event.
The interpretation of the force majeure clause within the Commercial Supply Agreement.
The calculation and quantum of damages for breach of contract under English law.
hiddenComplexities: The specific wording and scope of the force majeure clause in the Commercial Supply Agreement will be critical.
The burden of proof for establishing a force majeure event and its causal link to non-performance.
Potential arguments regarding foreseeability of the 'global shortage'.
Any notice requirements for invoking force majeure.

mootIntelligence.mostContestedArea: The applicability and interpretation of the force majeure clause.
mootIntelligence.mostVulnerableArea: Stark Industries Inc.'s ability to prove that the 'global shortage' meets the contractual definition of force majeure and that it was the sole cause of non-performance.
mostImportantFacts: The existence and terms of the Commercial Supply Agreement.
The specific wording of the arbitration clause and force majeure clause.
The failure to deliver vibranium cores by the deadline.
The claim of 'global shortage' as the basis for force majeure.
factsLikelyToBeAttacked: The assertion that a 'global shortage' constitutes a force majeure event under the contract.
The causal link between the 'global shortage' and Stark Industries Inc.'s inability to deliver.
The extent to which Stark Industries Inc. attempted to mitigate the shortage.
